items.text: Well logging is a detailed record of the geological formations penetrated by a borehole.
items.quote: making a detailed record (a well log) of the geologic formations penetrated by a borehole

items.text: The log may be based on visual inspection of recovered samples or on physical measurements made by instruments in the borehole.
items.quote: either on visual inspection of samples brought to the surface (geological logs) or on physical measurements made by instruments lowered into the hole (geophysical logs)

items.text: Some geophysical well-logging measurements can be performed at any stage in a well’s history: during drilling, well development, production, or abandonment.
items.quote: during any phase of a well's history: drilling, completing, producing, or abandoning

items.text: Well logging is used in the exploration for oil and gas, groundwater, mineral resources, and geothermal resources, as well as in environmental, scientific, and geotechnical studies.
items.quote: performed in boreholes drilled for the oil and gas, groundwater, mineral and geothermal exploration, as well as part of environmental, scientific and geotechnical studies

items.text: Wireline logging is used in mining, the oil and gas industry, and groundwater consulting to obtain a continuous record of rock properties.
items.quote: uses wireline logging to obtain a continuous record of a formation's rock properties

items.text: Wireline logging is defined as obtaining and analyzing geophysical data as a function of well depth, with the provision of related services.
items.quote: The acquisition and analysis of geophysical data performed as a function of well bore depth, together with the provision of related services.

items.text: Wireline logging and gas logging are different methods, but they are closely linked through the integration of data sets.
items.quote: "wireline logging" and "mud logging" are not the same, yet are closely linked through the integration of the data sets

items.text: Measurements are referenced to true depth along the hole (TAH).
items.quote: The measurements are made referenced to "TAH" - True Along Hole depth

items.text: It was directly measured that measurements and their analysis make it possible to infer additional properties, such as hydrocarbon saturation and reservoir pressure, and make decisions about drilling and production.
items.quote: used to infer further properties, such as hydrocarbon saturation and formation pressure, and to make further drilling and production decisions

items.text: A logging tool or tool assembly is lowered into the well on the end of a wireline cable.
items.quote: lowering a 'logging tool' - or a string of one or more instruments - on the end of a wireline into an oil well

items.text: Petrophysical properties are recorded using various sensors.
items.quote: recording petrophysical properties using a variety of sensors

items.text: It was directly measured that the instruments measure, among other things, natural gamma radiation, electrical and acoustic properties, induced radioactive responses, electromagnetic characteristics, NMR, and pressure.
items.quote: measure the natural gamma ray, electrical, acoustic, stimulated radioactive responses, electromagnetic, nuclear magnetic resonance, pressure and other properties

items.text: Logging can be conducted while drilling to obtain information about the formations being penetrated in real time.
items.quote: during the drilling process (see Logging While Drilling), to provide real-time information about the formations being penetrated by the borehole

items.text: Logging can also be performed after the well has reached its total depth, recording the entire borehole.
items.quote: once the well has reached Total Depth and the whole depth of the borehole can be logged

items.text: Visualization methods include optical, acoustic, and electrical imaging, as well as methods that combine acoustic and electrical techniques in a single logging tool.
items.quote: Methods that draw on both acoustic and electrical imaging techniques using the same logging tool

items.text: The depth recorded in memory mode can be corrected in the same way as real-time data, so the achievable TAH accuracy should not differ.
items.quote: so there should be no difference in the attainable TAH accuracy

items.text: Measurements must be corrected for elastic elongation and temperature.
items.quote: corrected for elastic stretch and temperature

items.text: Wireline logs can be classified by function or by the technology used.
items.quote: categorized either by their function or by the technology that they use

items.text: Logging in a cased well is conducted after the installation of the casing or production string.
items.quote: "Cased hole logs" are run after the well is lined with casing or production pipe.

items.text: Conrad and Marcel Schlumberger, who founded Schlumberger Limited in 1926, are considered the inventors of electrical logging.
items.quote: who founded Schlumberger Limited in 1926, are considered the inventors of electric well logging

items.text: It was directly measured that conrad developed the Schlumberger array for prospecting metallic ores, and the brothers adapted this surface method for underground measurements.
items.quote: a technique for prospecting for metal ore deposits, and the brothers adapted that surface technique to subsurface applications

items.text: In 1931, Henri Georges Doll and G. Deschâtres noticed that the galvanometer oscillated even without passing current through the cables in the borehole.
items.quote: the galvanometer wiggled even when no current was being passed through the logging cables down in  the well

items.text: The joint recording of SP and resistivity made it possible to distinguish permeable oil-bearing formations from impermeable nonproductive formations.
items.quote: By simultaneously recording SP and resistivity, loggers could distinguish between permeable oil-bearing beds and impermeable nonproducing beds.

items.text: Later, the basic dipmeter was improved with the resistivity dipmeter in 1947 and the continuous resistivity dipmeter in 1952.
items.quote: enhanced by the resistivity dipmeter (1947) and the continuous resistivity dipmeter (1952)

items.text: Conventional electrical logging methods require a conductive aqueous solution, whereas oil-based solutions do not conduct electricity.
items.quote: Normal electric logs require a conductive or water-based mud, but OBMs are nonconductive.

items.text: To address this problem, induction logging was developed in the late 19400s.
items.quote: The solution to this problem was the induction log, developed in the late 1940s.

items.text: Computerization accelerated the processing of logging data and sharply expanded the possibilities for collecting them.
items.quote: Computerization allowed much faster log processing, and dramatically expanded log data-gathering capacity.

items.text: In the 1970s, combined logs appeared in which resistivity and porosity logging were performed in a single pass through the well.
items.quote: combo type logs where resistivity logs and porosity logs were recorded in one pass in the borehole

items.text: Acoustic logging developed from technologies created during World War II.
items.quote: Sonic logs grew out of technology developed during World War II.

items.text: Initially, nuclear logging was developed to measure the natural gamma radiation of subsurface formations.
items.quote: Nuclear logging was initially developed to measure the natural gamma radiation emitted by underground formations.

items.text: Then the industry quickly moved to methods that actively irradiate rocks with nuclear particles.
items.quote: the industry quickly moved to logs that actively bombard rocks with nuclear particles

items.text: It was directly measured that gamma-ray logging, which measures natural radioactivity, appeared in 1939, and WSI neutron logging in 1941.
items.quote: The gamma ray log, measuring the natural radioactivity, was introduced by Well Surveys Inc. in 1939, and the WSI neutron log came in 1941.

items.text: Nuclear logs are important because they can be run in cased wells.
items.quote: These logs were important because they can be used in cased wells (wells with production casing).

items.text: During World War II, the U.S. government granted Schlumberger an almost complete monopoly on open-hole logging, and Lane-Wells a monopoly on cased-hole logging.
items.quote: The US Government gave a near wartime monopoly on open-hole logging to Schlumberger, and a monopoly on cased-hole logging to Lane-Wells.

items.text: It was directly measured that nuclear logging methods continued to develop after the war.
items.quote: Nuclear logs continued to evolve after the war.

items.text: Nicolas Bloembergen filed a patent for Schlumberger in 1966.
items.quote: Nicolaas Bloembergen filed the Schlumberger patent in 1966.

items.text: NUMAR's developments in the 19900s led to the creation of continuous NMR logging technology, used in the oil and gas industry, water exploration, and ore exploration.
items.quote: More recent engineering developments by NUMAR (a subsidiary of Halliburton) in the 1990s has resulted in continuous NMR logging technology

items.text: Many modern oil and gas wells are drilled directionally.
items.quote: Many modern oil and gas wells are drilled directionally.

items.text: Initially, when a well deviated from vertical, instruments had to be attached to the drill string somehow.
items.quote: loggers had to run their tools somehow attached to the drill pipe if the well was not vertical

items.text: Modern methods allow information to be transmitted continuously to the surface; this is called logging while drilling (LWD) or measurements while drilling (MWD).
items.quote: Modern techniques now permit continuous information at the surface.  This is known as logging while drilling (LWD) or measurement-while-drilling (MWD).

items.text: MWD transmits data from instruments at the bottom of the drill string to surface processors using mud pulses.
items.quote: MWD logs use mud pulse technology to transmit data from the tools on the bottom of the drillstring to the processors at the surface.

items.text: Instruments can be conveyed into wells with a deviated trajectory or with a reach exceeding that of conventional electric cables.
items.quote: The tools can be conveyed into wells where the trajectory is deviated or extended beyond the reach of conventional Electric Wireline cables.

items.text: For such wells, they may use a combination determined by the relationship between the mass and strength of the electric cable at a large reach.
items.quote: This can involve a combination of weight to strength ratio of the electric cable over this extended reach.

items.text: In such cases, memory tools can be conveyed on drill pipes or coiled tubing.
items.quote: the memory tools can be conveyed on Pipe or Coil Tubing

items.text: Compared with electric-line cable, memory logging sensors are limited in type and are usually intended for cased wells during the production stage.
items.quote: The type of sensors are limited in comparison to those used on Electric Line, and tend to be focussed on the cased hole, production stage of the well.

items.text: Compact instrument combinations have been developed for evaluating formations in an open hole, with data recorded in memory.
items.quote: Although there are now developed some memory "Open Hole" compact formation evaluation tool combinations.

items.text: Instruments can be lowered inside the drill pipe to protect them from damage while being lowered into the well.
items.quote: These tools can be deployed and carried downhole concealed internally in drill pipe to protect them from damage while running in the hole,

items.text: At depth, the instruments can be pushed out of the end of the drill pipe to begin logging.
items.quote: and then "Pumped" out the end at depth to initiate logging.

items.text: Other simple open-hole evaluation tools with memory recording that operate on slickline are also available for the production interval.
items.quote: Other basic open hole formation evaluation memory tools are available for use in "Commodity" markets on slickline

items.text: The use of such tools on slickline is intended to reduce the cost and time of operations.
items.quote: on slickline to reduce costs and operating time.

items.text: During operations in a cased well, a slickline unit is usually used for well intervention.
items.quote: In cased hole operation there is normally a "Slick Line" intervention unit.

items.text: It was directly measured that slickline uses solid mechanical wire with an outer diameter of 0.072–0.125 inches.
items.quote: This uses a solid mechanical wire (0.072 - 0.125 inches in OD),

items.text: It was directly measured that this wire is used to manipulate the well completion system or perform other operations in it.
items.quote: to manipulate or otherwise carry out operations in the well bore completion system.

items.text: Operations with memory tools are always conducted on slickline instead of mobilizing a full-scale electric logging unit.
items.quote: Memory operations are often carried out on this Slickline conveyance in preference to mobilizing a full service Electric Wireline unit.

items.text: The results of memory logging become known only after the instruments return to the surface.
items.quote: Since the results are not known until returned to surface,

items.text: This limits the ability to precisely change downhole production conditions during memory logging by regulating surface flow rates.
items.quote: This limits the ability to modify or change the well down hole production conditions accurately during the memory logging by changing the surface production rates.

items.text: A malfunction during recording is detected only after the memory devices are removed.
items.quote: Failure during recording is not known until the memory tools are retrieved.

items.text: Data loss can become a serious problem on large and expensive marine facilities.
items.quote: This loss of data can be a major issue on large offshore (expensive) locations.

items.text: At onshore sites, for example in South Texas, where the commodity segment of the oilfield services sector operates, logging is always conducted without the infrastructure of a drilling rig.
items.quote: On land locations (e.g. South Texas, US) where there is what is called a "Commodity" Oil service sector, where logging often is without the rig infrastructure.

items.text: Under the described land-based conditions, data loss is more problematic, and logging is often repeated without complications.
items.quote: this is less problematic, and logs are often run again without issue.
